newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill rates higher but players sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill rates higher but players sidelined.

text.p: Manila banks quoted higher bid and offer rates for Treasury bills in the secondary market after a two percentage-point increase in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 32 percent, traders said.
But banks stayed on the sidelines after the recent volatility in interest rates, traders said.
The Central Bank raised again its rate for the fourth time in more than a week after the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht.
"We're recuperating from third degree burns," a dealer said, after the heavy selling of bills yesterday.
A Reuters poll of six financial institutions gave offers of 12.125/12.625 percent for the three-month bills; 12.625/12.90 percent for the six months; and 13.15/13.50 percent for the one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate jumped to 32.15625 percent from 30.375 percent in step with the Central Bank's rate hike.
Volume was at 14.54 billion pesos, with 35 lenders and 11 borrowers.
